turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Afternoon. Sit. What did you come for?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, ja, hi. Sorry, I'm a bit all over the place. I came to ask if I can drive again.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Last seizure?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Two years, hey. No fits since then. I'm thirty four, epilepsy since I was twenty two, on the kepra.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): There's more. Tell him properly.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, she's going to make a thing of it. It wasn't a fit.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did you see?
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last month, sometime, I can't pin the day, eish. We stopped at a robot and he went blank, stared, didn't answer, about a minute, then carried on like nothing.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't remember a blank spell. I was tired, that's all. It was not a seizure.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tablets. Still on levetiracetam?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, levetirasetam, by mouth, seven fifty milligrams twice a day. Been on it five years.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Missed any?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, when we travelled to Durban for the wedding the bottle was in the other bag. I did miss some evenings.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was two or three evenings, and some mornings when he's late for deliveries he skips it as well.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not the mornings. Maybe two evenings, maybe three, I honestly don't know. Not a regular thing.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever at all.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough, tight chest, trouble breathing?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest is fine, hey.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No headaches.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight gone up or down?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nurse left the vitals. Pressure one oh six over seventy seven.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She said one oh nine over seventy seven. I heard her read it.

[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ja. Chart is one oh nine over seventy seven. I misread it. Pulse seventy two. Weight seventy one kilograms today. Last time in March you were sixty eight kilos, and your last pressure was one forty over eighty eight.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Is one oh nine ok? Does the March one mean I'm worse? Can I drive the bakkie for work if it's only short trips, like to the robot and back?
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today's pressure is fine. I am not signing you fit to drive.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Why? Two years is two years. My boss will lose it. Will the medical aid even pay for a letter? What if I drive slow?
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): That spell might have been a small seizure, an absence, or you were just tired and zoned out. I can't tell which. Missed tablets make a seizure more likely. No driving.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So do I take an extra tablet to catch up? Is one miss enough to cause it? Am I going backwards with the epilepsy?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): No extra tablets. Same seven fifty twice a day, every day, including when you travel. Epilepsy is still the diagnosis. Don't double up.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok ok. Do I need bloods? Does the needle hurt, how many tubes, will medical aid pay or must I pay cash?
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): One blood test, a levetiracetam level. I'll book it. Come back in three weeks for the result.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks is hectic. What if I blank out again at work before that? Can my sister bring me sooner?
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you have another blank spell, come straight in. Otherwise three weeks. No driving till I say, not even a short one.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll bring him. He lives with me and his sister since that Durban trip.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I live with them. It's alright. Must I bring the pill bottle? The chemist label is half rubbed off.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bring the bottle next time. She drives. You don't.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): If the level is low will you put the dose up? And kepra is the same as levetirasetam, right? I read it makes people angry. Am I getting angry? Sorry, too many questions.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Same drug. I'm not changing the dose today. You haven't said you're irritable, so leave the internet. We see the level first.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Sharp. And if the test is normal can I get the driving letter then? Just now, or only after three weeks?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today, and not automatically. Three weeks, we look, then we talk about the form. Reception books the bloods and the visit.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Shame, thanks. I'll try not to panic. Eish.

spec.situation: Adult with epilepsy on levetiracetam, seizure-free for two years, asks about driving; missed doses when travelling; relative saw a 'blank spell' last month; doctor reviews and plans a blood test.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Last seizure/fit was two years ago; no fits since then.
Patient asked whether he can drive again and specifically whether he can drive the work bakkie for short trips; doctor explicitly refused to sign him fit to drive.
Missed levetiracetam doses occurred during travel to Durban for a wedding because the bottle was in another bag.
Caregiver reported he skipped some morning levetiracetam doses when late for deliveries, which the patient denied.
Negative finding: no chest tightness and no trouble breathing were specifically asked and denied.
Weight trend/history: current weight 71 kg, previously 68 kg in March.
Prior blood pressure was 140/88 at the last visit in March.
Doctor advised not to double up/catch up missed doses: no extra tablets after a missed dose.
Doctor stated epilepsy remains the diagnosis.
Follow-up instruction was to come straight in if another blank spell occurs, not merely sometime later.
Reception was to book both the blood test and the follow-up visit.
Doctor said he is not changing the levetiracetam dose today and will wait for the drug level first.
Doctor said a normal levetiracetam level would not automatically result in a driving letter; reassessment would occur at the three-week visit.
